A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, figures, tables, prompts, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite appendix reordering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 23 LLM judges, comparisons of GPT-4.1-generated speeches with human speeches, and analyses of prompting, ensembling, and judge explanations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports a GPT-4.1 repeated-run stability experiment in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The zero-shot and CoT judging prompts, score parsing, ensembling, GPT-4.1 speech generation, and key-point analysis procedures are retained. Expanded explanations do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 631 benchmark speeches across 76 topics and 152 additional GPT-4.1 speeches. Expanded annotation provenance concerns the existing dataset; few-shot prompting and multi-turn evaluation remain future work.

E2.justification: The same 23 judge models, human reference judgments, CoT comparisons, and ensemble constituents remain evaluated. The five judges comparing GPT-4.1 and human speeches in Figure 6 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The data partition, 50-shared-speech threshold, agreement metrics, prompts, quantization, and generation settings remain unchanged. The new replication repeats the existing judging protocol; its run counts and variability reporting are statistical additions.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds a small GPT-4.1 replication testing whether low-temperature judging remains stable across repeated runs. Existing CoT, parsing-error, ensembling, source-level, and key-point analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 newly states that the main results use one run per judge and reports a separate GPT-4.1 check with three runs per speech. v1 provides neither this run-count disclosure nor the between-run variability assessment; this does not establish increased replication for the main comparisons.

E6.justification: v2 adds the finding that GPT-4.1 Tau and Kappa vary by no more than ±0.003 across repeated runs. Appendix C.1 also newly quotes the original dataset's κ = 0.24, explicitly attributed to Slonim et al. Existing plotted results, rankings, tables, and speech examples remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version presents new theorems or proofs. v2 clarifies the existing agreement measures and evaluation rationale without changing mathematical definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: debate-speech evaluation as a benchmark, partial alignment between capable LLM and human judges, systematic judging differences, and potentially human-surpassing speech generation.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive caveats about shared prompts favoring some models and quantization potentially affecting performance. Expanded future-work discussion distinguishes updated knowledge from improved reasoning and considers prompt adaptation. The central interpretations and existing stylistic-bias caveat remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds documentation of the existing dataset's recording provenance, crowd-annotation instructions, source blinding, control questions, and manual quality review. Hyperparameters, speech truncation, and code/data access information are retained; these additions document prior collection procedures rather than new data collection.

R1.justification: v2 adds Mirkin et al. (2018) as a source for recorded human debates. Most other reference changes update publication metadata, while the main positioning against earlier judging and debate-evaluation research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language and metric-explanation edits, expands future work and limitations, and reorders Appendices A–C while subdividing the dataset documentation. Most of the main narrative and remaining appendices are retained.

P2.justification: All 19 figures and two tables are retained, with unchanged plots. Figure 2b's subcaption and Figure 5's caption are clarified, and appendix figures and Table 2 are rearranged through the revised layout.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through fuller annotation provenance, clearer agreement explanations, explicit single-run disclosure, and a limited repeatability check. Added prompt and quantization caveats improve qualification of the findings. These are useful but bounded gains: the core evidence is unchanged, and the repeatability check covers only one judge.
